function.description: Executes a given command using the os.system() function specifically for Windows operating systems. For multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For complex tasks, create and run a .bat file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The Windows command line instruction(s) to be executed. Use '&&' between commands for multiple instructions. For complex sequences, encapsulate the logic within a .bat file and provide the execution command here.

message.reasoning: The user says: "start Docker on window using docker start." They want to start Docker on Windows using docker start. But docker start is used to start containers, not the Docker daemon. To start Docker service, you need to start Docker Desktop or the Docker Engine service. On Windows, you can use "net start com.docker.service" or "Start-Service -Name com.docker.service" in PowerShell. Or "docker-machine start default" if using Docker Machine. But the user likely wants to start Docker Desktop. We can use "Start-Service com.docker.service". Let's use PowerShell command: "Start-Service -Name com.docker.service". Or "net start com.docker.service". We'll use the cmd_controller_execute function to run the command. We'll provide the command string. Use "powershell -Command \"Start-Service -Name com.docker.service\"" or "net start com.docker.service". Let's choose "net start com.docker.service". We'll call the function.
